catalog_locator: p. 128 (PDF page 6 of 21), section 4.2 'Lexical contrasts'; saved file the copy we hold, text layer page image
catalog_quote: Avikam has two contrastive lexical tones, High and Low. It has also a downstepped High tone. There are no contrastive lexical Mid tones. The language has no contrastive contour tones on monosyllables, though it has, according to Hérault (1982:267), High-Low and Low-High contours on some syllables in initial, medial and final positions. In verbs, contour tones are clearly derived tones. A short glance at the lexicon (as for instance given in Hérault's (1982) Atlas, volume 2) provides minimal pairs of level tones. As mentioned above, CV words don't occur in isolation, so the contrastive pairs have all a prefix vowel. ... It should be noted that a High in a Low High sequence as in (1) is not automatically downstepped. The Downstep can be analysed as a floating tone that lowers following High tones but its position is not predictable, though it generally occurs word internally as in (2)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.rule_in_words: Avikam is a two-tone language (H, L, plus downstepped H) with lexical tonal minimal pairs; the article's prosodic constituents (tonal foot, prosodic word, phonological phrase) are defined by a Tone Lowering rule, and no word stress or accent is mentioned at all.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress; the tonal statement notes downstep position is unpredictable and surface contours (HL, LH) occur on some syllables per Hérault 1982:267.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical word (citation forms carry a prefix vowel; CV roots do not occur in isolation); the article is about tone across words and phrases in the Kpanda dialect of Grand Lahou.
new_statements.identity_note: Ahoua 2009 describes the Kpanda dialect of Avikam (Grand Lahou coast, fieldwork 1999); he notes at least two dialects differing only in minor segmental correspondences. Same language-level glottocode avik1243; no separate dialect glottocode found.
